findings.message: This round changes the update card so its From/Owner line resolves the owner's name from auth.user. That fixes the round-1 finding about the card's From line, but no test drives the card. The new table test in proposal-agent.test.ts renders only ProposalPage and ProposalsTable. Neither the card's 'From' and 'Owner → who' lines nor the ProjectPage board card's Avatar name, which this diff also changes, is checked across the four owner variants. Fix: extend the AC-1 it.each to call moveCard/updateProposalCard (or whichever card builder reads proposalNow) and render ProjectPage, asserting 'Unassigned' only for the 'neither' row and 'Maya Fernando' for the 'a user only' row.
findings.scenario: Revert the coalesce in proposalNow. With owner_user_id = maya and owner_name = null, the reassign card says 'From: Unassigned'. The suite still passes.

findings.message: The rule for which owner name to show is written twice as raw SQL: `coalesce(p.owner_name, (select u.name from auth.user u where u.id = p.owner_user_id))` appears here and again in queries.ts:57 (owner_shown). This round adds one place for the withdrawn rule (withdrawnIn), but the owner-name rule gets two copies that can drift apart. Fix: export one SQL fragment, e.g. `ownerShownIn("p")` in readiness.ts or owner.ts, and use it in both queries.

This round says there is now one withdrawn rule (`isWithdrawn` / `withdrawnIn`), but two copies of the rule are left, and both test `meta.withdrawn` for truthiness: `SpecFacts` (`m.withdrawn ? "withdrawn"`) and the sync's withdraw pass (`modules/delivery/sync/import.ts:79`, `if (meta.withdrawn) continue`). The new rule counts a proposal as withdrawn only when the value reads as the text "true". These copies count any truthy value. Fix: use `isWithdrawn(p)` in SpecFacts (and `p.withdrawn` from the row) and `isWithdrawn(cur)` in import.ts, so all four paths read one rule.
findings.scenario: A spec proposal has `meta.withdrawn = "false"` (or `1`). `isWithdrawn` and `ACTIVE` treat it as open, so it shows in lists and the board and takes task closes. But its board card shows the "withdrawn" chip, and when its folder is removed from the repo, import.ts skips it, so it is never marked withdrawn and stays active.

findings.message: Because hasNoOwner treats owner_user_id alone as owned, a row whose owner_user_id no longer finds a named auth.user (the user was removed, or the name is null) now shows an empty Owner cell. ProposalPage shows an empty , and ProjectPage's Avatar gets name "". Before this change these rows showed 'Unassigned'. A name that can't be resolved should show as unknown, not as a blank. Fix: when ownerUserId is set and ownerName is null, render a 'Unknown person' label or similar.
findings.scenario: owner_user_id = <id with no auth.user row>, owner_name = null → the Owner column is blank and the proposal page shows an empty bold owner.
